summary: Report No. 32 covers May 1948, prepared by the National Economic Board. Its Summary calls the month historic: the 10 May general election (over 91 per cent of registrants voting despite communist terror) and the 31 May opening of the National Assembly, which elected Syngman Rhee Speaker. North Korea cut electricity to the South on 14 May, discrediting Kim Koo and Kimm Kiu-sic after the Pyongyang conference and cutting industrial output sharply. The text also covers Cheju-do guerrilla fighting, 38th Parallel incidents, Mukden repatriation, vested property sales, farmland transfers, drought, finance, public works, police, education, culture and youth/women's groups. Caution for researchers: the scan is misbound. PDF pages 47-113 and 134-137 are pages of a July 1947 report (Legislative Assembly debates, constitution draft, Joint Commission, police and prison tables), replacing May 1948 material on industry, mining, allocations, trade, labor, transportation, communications and loans.
highlights: 10 May 1948: first general election, with over 91 per cent of registrants voting despite communist terror; 198 Assembly members were elected, and Cheju-do's Puk Cheju A and B districts were postponed.
31 May: the National Assembly opened with all 198 members, and Syngman Rhee was elected Speaker with 188 votes.
14 May: North Korea cut the electric power that supplied about 60 per cent of South Korea's electricity; national distribution fell from 74.5 to 56.1 million KWH and overall production fell sharply.
Kim Koo and Kimm Kiu-sic lost political standing after their Pyongyang assurance that power would continue proved false.
By 31 May, 448,513 of 587,974 farms (76 per cent) of former Japanese farmland had been sold or transferred to Koreans through the National Land Administration.
The first Mukden repatriates reached Inchon by LST from Tientsin on 10-11 May; 3,831 had been repatriated by month's end and 2,651 were still awaiting passage.
Election violence left a press tally of 202 dead and 643 wounded, and the Cheju-do rebellion intensified, with 3,126 persons held; police reported 68 of 13,407 polling booths attacked.
Ordinance No. 192 separated the courts from the Department of Justice effective 1 June 1948; the scan is also misbound, with July 1947 pages replacing May 1948 industry, labor and transport sections.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover (No. 32, May 1948, National Economic Board), blank page, list of Board members at 31 May 1948, and four-page table of contents.

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: Overview of May: the 10 May election, the 14 May power cutoff and falling output, drought, fertilizer, population growth, border and Cheju-do violence, fear of Japan, public works, vested property, trade and finance.

sections.title: Part I: Basic Aspects
sections.summary: Population and migration (20.0 million by January 1948), Mukden repatriation, draft immigration ordinance, and Office of Property Custody preparations for Koreanization of vested property.

sections.title: Section 1: Population and Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: South Korea's population rose one-third since 1940 to 20.0 million by January 1948; 2.4 million entered against 886,000 leaving. Covers Mukden repatriates, Korean schools in Japan and a draft immigration ordinance.

sections.title: Census Report
sections.summary: Compares 1940, 1944, 1946 and 1948 counts; natural increase revised to 1.8 per cent; urban population up 72.7 per cent since 1940.

sections.title: Population Migration
sections.summary: Table by province and cumulative movement tables; refugee arrivals from the North fell about 20 per cent from April to May (12,391).

sections.title: Manchurian Repatriates
sections.summary: First Mukden repatriates reached Inchon by LST from Tientsin on 11 May; 3,831 repatriated by month's end, 2,651 still awaiting; LARA aid.

sections.title: Korean Education in Japan
sections.summary: Dispute between the Korean League and the Japanese government over Korean schools; CI&E proposals on textbooks and teachers; Osaka and Kobe disturbances halted talks.

sections.title: Repatriation of Korean Businessmen from Japan
sections.summary: Korean businessmen in Japan increasingly applied to return; the 1,000-won allowance and property-shipment limits had slowed repatriation.

sections.title: Immigration and Emigration Regulations
sections.summary: Digest of a new ordinance replacing Ordinance No. 49 (due about 1 August 1948): entry documents, Home Affairs Bureaus as agents, definition of Korean citizen, exempt aliens.

sections.title: Section 2: Vested Property
sections.summary: Office of Property Custody prepared for Koreanization: a record 2,334 financial statements, reorganization studies, rising sales applications after the election, rent collection. Page 27 is garbled OCR.

sections.title: Operations
sections.summary: Took over the Korean Residence Management Corporation on 6 May; investigated 1,841 companies for reorganization, 484 unlocated; loan guarantees status reviewed.

sections.title: Property Disposal
sections.summary: Post-election rise in purchase applications (497 cases in May); tables of appraisals and sales, with May total 111 million won.

sections.title: Real Estate Section
sections.summary: 63 dependent houses and 11 Army parcels released; condition surveys arranged with Camp Seoul.

sections.title: Comptroller Division
sections.summary: Training Korean auditors, handbook, bilingual reports, new tax forms, Budget Section and bank-deposit reconciliation.

sections.title: Rental Properties
sections.summary: Full lease report as of 31 December 1947; table of new leases and rents collected January-April 1948 (2,252 new leases in April).

sections.title: Property of Allied Nationals
sections.summary: Japanese Custodian records checked for Allied-owned property; US-owned cases go to the State Department or to claims against Japan.

sections.title: Executive Division
sections.summary: Collected synopses and narrative reports from all SKIG agencies toward a general inventory of vested property.

sections.title: Part II: Production and Supply

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Insufficient spring rainfall likely to cut summer grain yields; final estimates redone in May.

sections.title: Bureau of Agricultural Economics
sections.summary: 5 May summer-grain forecast tables 1930-1948; 1,847 Crop Reporting Service staff appointed, 37 resignations over pay.

sections.title: Bureau of Agricultural Production
sections.summary: Livestock, poultry feed, fertilizer allocations, cotton stocks of 7,578 tons, sericulture, power-pump irrigation (94,153 acres), sweet and Irish potatoes.

sections.title: Bureau of Forestry
sections.summary: 16 million acres of forestland; annual cut exceeds growth; reforestation fell from 358 million trees (1942) to 61.6 million (1947); charcoal, fuelwood and log tables.

sections.title: Bureau of Fisheries
sections.summary: Exports to Japan Sept 1947-May 1948 worth $4.9 million (laver, anchovies, seaweed); landings expected near pre-war levels after fleet reorganization.

sections.title: Korea Agricultural Association
sections.summary: Fertilizer receipts and sales (156,444 and 106,717 tons in 1948), US imports replacing Japan, 10,000 tons ammonium sulphate from the North by barter; straw bag and rope purchases.

sections.title: National Land Administration
sections.summary: 448,513 of 587,974 farms sold or transferred by 31 May (76 per cent), with table by regional office; surveys ordered for deeds.

sections.title: Agricultural Improvement Service
sections.summary: Rice experiment projects seeded; Pusan Fisheries College placed under AIS for administration.

sections.title: Section 2: Prices

sections.title: Wholesale and Retail Prices
sections.summary: Indexes (August 1945 = 100) for 27 wholesale and 26 retail commodities to May 1948; grain shortage lifted food prices.

sections.summary: National Price Administration prices of controlled domestic goods; nine-city open-market retail prices; price and production trend charts.

sections.summary: Power cutoff and drought hurt water pumping at Inchon and elsewhere; emergency measures taken.

sections.title: Fire Control
sections.summary: 181 fires in May, 37 by arson, with loss of 251.7 million won; industrial fire survey; extinguishing supplies received.

sections.summary: Four weekly meetings in May and a list of items acted on, including daylight saving time from 31 May and telephone rates.

sections.summary: Four-day provincial officers' convention from 16 May; warning about abuse of eligible lists; general pay raise averaging 50 per cent.

sections.summary: Table of personnel October 1946-May 1948; civilian turnover high due to one-year contracts.

sections.summary: The 10 May election and 198-member Assembly (tables by province, party, occupation), Rhee's statements, 31 May opening, North-South Conference, the 14 May power shut-off and Koreans in Japan.

sections.title: General

sections.summary: Results by province with names, ages and parties of the 198 members; party and occupation tables; reactions of rightist and moderate parties and Kim Koo; average age 47.

sections.summary: South Korean parties protested for months over Japan's treatment of Koreans, claiming Japanese imperialism was being revived; closure of Korean schools in Japan was seen as an infringement of Korean rights.

sections.summary: Ordinances Nos. 192-197 (court reorganization first), daylight saving proclamation, four legal opinions on vested property, prisons (22,141 inmates), courts and Cheju-do trial team.

sections.title: Ordinances and Orders
sections.summary: Ordinance 192 Court Reorganization through Ordinance 197 (Coast Guard searches); daylight saving from 31 May; proclamation on the National Assembly; summer grain collection.

sections.title: Legal Opinions
sections.summary: Opinions on SKIG claims for vested property damage, the Chosun Aircraft board election, Seoul city property powers, and the free silk market.

sections.summary: Drafting of the Air Carriers section of the proposed Korean Civil Code was completed in May, with articles on definitions, rights, jurisdiction, liability and operation.

sections.title: Property Claims Commission
sections.summary: Simplified procedure directive of 17 April 1948 for vested property claims.
